correctness.rationale: The stationary transport solution i=J*S is uniquely determined and belongs to the declared L1 phase space exactly when J=0 or m=integral(S)<infinity. Direct algebraic elimination then gives R0>1 and all positive coordinates uniquely; conversely each displayed solution satisfies every stationary equation. S derivative yields sigma=1-S(infinity). An integrable positive hazard forces S(infinity)>0. For k/(1+a), m=1/(k-1) exactly for k>1. The characteristics identity has a bounded initial contribution, and a convolution splitting proves M/K -> j only under the explicitly stated condition J(t)->j>0. The unconditional S(infinity)-weighted incidence lower bound is immediate. Exact symbolic/rational replay corroborates algebra; no finite experiment serves as the proof of any infinite claim.

originality.rationale: The specific published 2025 paper gives a positive equilibrium formula under positive bounded integrable hazard and claims existence for R0>1, without reconciling nonzero S(infinity) with its L1 phase space. The new result supplies the missing necessary-and-sufficient condition, a constant-R0 tail-exponent phase boundary and precisely qualified mass escape. Earlier general survival-formula and positive-baseline-mortality theory are explicitly credited, not claimed novel. Four implication-level comparisons and relevant primary full texts were examined; unindexed overlap is a residual risk.
residual_risks: The general renewal fact that stationary occupancy equals incidence times mean survival is older than this application; the novelty is restricted to its exact application and contradiction of the 2025 stated L1 existence test.
Published search and indexed mathematical records may miss unindexed source-specific corrections or parallel observations.
No numerical simulation of the source is used to infer infinite-age behavior or global dynamics.

value.rationale: The newly infected, not-yet-transactivated HIV reservoir is a biologically meaningful unbounded-age compartment. The expected residence time, not just eventual activation probability or R0, determines whether a finite-mass endemic state is meaningful. The criterion corrects a concrete functional-space gap in a published existence theorem, provides a sharp heavy-tail k=1 phase boundary at fixed R0, and gives an exact retention/mass-growth identity relevant to interpretation of long-age truncations. This goes beyond a standalone cheap normalization test.
